findings.title: Agent TCP length prefix completely unchecked → stack overflow before crypto
findings.description: On TCP, the agent reads a plaintext int32_t length then recv()s that many bytes into buffer[OS_MAXSTR+1] with no check that 1 <= length <= OS_MAXSTR. Remoted rejects length > OS_MAXSTR; the agent rejects nothing. Framing is processed before Blowfish/ReadSecMSG. Positive oversized lengths (e.g. 7000) that remoted would drop overflow the agent stack. length==OS_MAXSTR+1 also makes buffer[recv_b]='\0' one past the array in receiver.c.
findings.impact: Crash or likely code execution as the agent user (Linux ossec/chroot; Windows LocalSystem) without the agent key — only MITM or manager-channel injection on TCP framing.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses protocol tcp.
2. Attacker is on-path or spoofs the manager.
3. Send 4-byte LE length 7000 then >=7000 payload bytes.
4. receive_msg/start_agent overflows buffer[OS_MAXSTR+1] before crypto.
findings.remediation: Require length > 0 && length <= OS_MAXSTR (and <= sizeof(buffer)-1 before NUL). Close socket on violation. Add the same lower bound in remoted.

findings.title: csyslogd field_add_string/truncated stack off-by-one and heap overflow on near-full alert buffer
findings.description: OS_Alert_SendSyslog builds into char syslog_msg[OS_SIZE_2048] (exactly 2048 bytes). After a large snprintf of location/comment, strlen can be 2047 so dest_sz/available_sz=1. field_add_string then strncat(dest, buffer, 1) writes a NUL at index 2048 (past the array). field_add_truncated with available_sz in {1,2,3} mallocs a 1–3 byte buffer, os_substr refuses non-positive length, then strcat(truncated, "...") overflows the heap chunk. Agent-controlled alert location/log can inflate the initial snprintf.
findings.impact: Stack off-by-one and/or small-heap overflow in ossec-csyslogd: crash (DoS of syslog forwarding) or plausible code execution as the csyslogd user when syslog_output is enabled.
findings.attack_path:
1. Enable <syslog_output>.
2. Registered agent produces alerts whose location/comment/log fill the 2047-byte header snprintf.
3. Later field_add_string/truncated run with available_sz in {1,2,3}.
4. Stack and/or heap corrupted.
findings.remediation: Size syslog_msg as OS_SIZE_2048+1 or pass sizeof. Use remaining=size-strlen(dest)-1. In field_add_truncated require field_sz > strlen(trailer) before strcat; prefer snprintf into the heap buffer.

findings.title: doDiff joins unsanitized syslog hostname into /queue/diff path enabling chroot write escape
findings.description: When lf->hostname does not start with '(', doDiff snprintfs DIFF_DIR/hostname/sigid/last-entry. hostname_map allows '/'. Stock rule 533 check_diff matches ossec: output: 'netstat -tan, and the ossec decoder prematches ^ossec: , so a syslog event with a traversal hostname and that body triggers _add2last mkdir/fopen/fwrite outside /queue/diff under the analysisd chroot. Distinct from the excluded last_events stack UAF.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated (when syslog remote + allowips permits) write of attacker log bytes under the OSSEC chroot as ossecr. Basename fixed as last-entry under <sigid>/.
findings.attack_path:
1. Enable remoted connection syslog with allowips including attacker.
2. Send syslog with hostname ../../tmp/pwn and body ossec: output: 'netstat -tan': crafted.
3. Rule 533 check_diff runs doDiff.
4. Chroot path /tmp/pwn/533/last-entry is written.
findings.remediation: Sanitize hostname for path use (reject '/', '..', non-allowlisted bytes) or hash/encode before joining under DIFF_DIR.
